chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ḥarīz, Fuḍayl, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, who said:
It was said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: For what reason is the palm-stalk placed with the deceased?
He said: “The punishment is kept away from him as long as it remains fresh.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Whoever is unable to place the palm-stalk with his deceased in his shrouds out of taqiyyah from the people of opposition and their disgraceful false accusations regarding it, then let him bury it with him in his grave. If he is not able to do that, or fears because of it for some reason among the reasons, then there is nothing upon him in leaving it, and Allah the Exalted accepts his excuse in the state of necessity.

key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةُ: the palm-stalk placed with the deceased
key_terms.الْعَذَابُ: punishment, here referring to punishment affecting the dead
key_terms.تَقِيَّةً: dissimulation for protection in circumstances of danger or harm
key_terms.رَطْبَةً: fresh or moist, describing the palm-stalk

ai.seo_question: Why is a fresh palm-stalk placed with the deceased in Shia burial practice, and what if it cannot be used?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the palm-stalk placed with the deceased serves as a means by which punishment is kept away so long as it remains fresh. It also records a legal ruling that if placing it in the shroud is not possible due to taqiyyah or necessity, it may be buried in the grave, and if even that is not possible, there is no blame in omitting it.
